wu: Health Charades: Students take turns acting out illnesses (e.g., coughing, holding a stomach) while others guess the illness in English. Props: None. They say 'You have a cold!' or 'You should see a doctor!'
wuAlt: Alternative warm-up 1: Illness Bingo with flashcards of body parts and symptoms. They mark off the words on their bingo cards as you call them out.
Alternative warm-up 2: Quick survey in pairs: 'What should you do if you have a headache?' They write one tip each.
pres: Show a cartoon of a teen with a stomachache. Model sentences: 'You shouldn't eat so much fast food.' 'You should drink water.' Check understanding with thumbs up/down: 'If you have a fever, should you go to school?'
presAlt: Alternative presentation 1: Use a role-play script where a doctor gives advice to a patient. Highlight 'should/shouldn't' in the dialogue.
Alternative presentation 2: Display a poster with 'good/bad' health habits. Elicit advice sentences from students using 'should/shouldn't'.
prac: Modal Match: Students match health problems (headache, sunburn) to advice (rest, use sunscreen) on cut-out cards. Then practice in pairs: 'If you have a headache, you should...'
pracAlt: Alternative practice 1: Advice Relay Race. Teams race to write correct advice sentences on the board for given problems.
Alternative practice 2: 'Should or Shouldn't?' card sort. Students sort sentences into two columns and justify their choices.
ls: Listen to a 2-minute podcast where teens discuss staying healthy. Students complete a table: 'Problem - Advice' (e.g., 'Problem: tired - Advice: sleep more'). Check answers in pairs.
re: Simon Says Health Edition: 'Simon says you should stretch!' or 'Simon says you shouldn't run with scissors!' Students move only when the command is correct.
prod: Health Panel Discussion: Groups of 3 play 'teen experts' (doctor, nutritionist, fitness coach) giving advice on a real teen issue (e.g., exam stress). Each student speaks for 2 minutes using 'should/ought to/had better'.
rw: Read a short health article about Ramadan fasting. Compare the advice using 'should/ought to/had better' in a table. Then write a 60-word email to a friend giving one piece of advice from the article.
st: Read a short story about a teen who follows bad advice and feels worse. End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we learned to give health advice. Thank you, class!'
g: Students draw health problems/advice while others guess in English.
Each student adds one piece of advice to a growing chain: 'You should drink water, and you shouldn't drink soda...'
Students replace 'should' with 'ought to' or 'had better' in sentences and check if meaning changes.
Teams answer questions like 'What should you do for a sore throat?' to win points.
Students pick a card (e.g., 'You have a cough') and give advice to a partner.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 'Top 5 Health Tips' list for teens using at least 3 modals.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'You should ____' or 'You shouldn't ____' for the production task.
hw: Homework option 1: Find a short health article online and write 3 advice sentences using 'should/shouldn't'.
Homework option 2: Record a 30-second video giving health advice to a friend.
Homework option 3: Write a 70-word paragraph about one health habit you should change.
tip: Encourage students to connect advice to local contexts, like staying hydrated during summer in Oujda or adjusting meals for Ramadan, to make the language relevant.
